title: Negative: a waste that remembers the eaters' trait distribution does not unbound the fed vortices' trait cloud; it stops new ground earlier than c58's mean-trait waste (2 seeds, T=10000)
summary: world.py = c58's trait3d fed vortices with wmode 'rff': the waste carries 24 random-feature masses ([cos, sin](w_m.theta)/sqrt(12), 12 orthogonal frequencies w_m ~ N(0, I/sw^2)), so G = sum_k phi_k(theta) U_k / W is the mean Gaussian similarity (sw 0.4) of a vortex's trait to the traits of past eaters rather than to their mean (kernel error 0.14 mean abs). Paired with c61's mean-waste and kind-blind runs on the same seeds and mutation draws, read with vcmp.py (vnov.py's units). Seed 6, standard waste, T=10000: cloud radius 0.32, 0.53, 0.61, 0.64, then 0.59-0.44 (mean waste 0.23 -> 1.21; twin 0.22-0.33); the hull (farthest trait from the ancestor) is frozen at 1.39 from t=3000 (mean waste 2.22); share on new ground 0.00-0.02 after t=5000. Seed 10, long memory (lifetime 2000 t): radius peaks at 0.78 (t=6000) and falls to 0.49; hull 1.81 vs 2.18; new ground 0.19, 0.15, 0.03, 0.00, 0.00 in the last five windows (mean waste ends at 0.01 too). Heredity and novelty counts stay above the twin (200 persistent splits, 165 daughters keep the class, generation 35; distinct dominants 9 and 11, first-time dominants after t=3000 5 and 8, against 7 and 9 for the mean waste to t=10000). With distribution memory the population holds 3-4 coexisting trait clusters (maps) instead of pushing out from its mean, so the prediction from Heyde and Mahadevan 2026 (20261028T0212) fails here: memory of the distribution, at these lifetimes, stabilizes a polymorphism in a bounded region.

finding.operator: kind-specific waste that stores the eaters' trait distribution (random features) instead of their mean trait
finding.control: c61's mean-waste arm and kind-blind twin on the same seeds and mutation draws (seed 6 standard, seed 10 long memory)
finding.result: seed 6: radius 0.49 vs 1.13 (mean) vs 0.32 (twin) at t=10000, hull frozen at 1.39 from t=3000, new ground <= 0.02 after t=5000; seed 10 (long memory): radius 0.49 vs 0.94 vs 0.45, hull 1.81 vs 2.18 vs 1.10, new ground 0.00 in the last two windows

limits: One frequency draw (rff_seed 0); the random-feature kernel is anisotropic with oscillating tails (direction-dependent revivals up to ~0.4 at |d| > 1), which can itself hold the cloud; a replicate with rff_seed 1 on seed 6 is running. Two seeds; mean-waste comparison runs are c61's. The feature masses are transported every 5 steps (nsub 5) with the source summed over them.
